title: Cap. III Rat. 10: mere beneplacitum makes works idle — Predestinati / Sigebertus
pass_a_gloss: Reason 10. If God, not having regard of merits, from his sole good pleasure had decreed to bless singular persons, for example Paul and Peter, since good works would operate nothing at all toward obtaining glory, Make therefore Peter walk in good works, yet glory will not be attributed to him from any merit toward such works: make him altogether neglect good works, God nevertheless by the force of his good pleasure will give him the destined glory: But this is very absurd, and leans toward the error of the Predestinarians, whom Sigebert in his Chronicle shows to have taught that to those living piously good works do not profit unto glory, if they be not Predestinated; to those living flagitiously no crimes harm, if they be of the predestinated.
pass_b_english: Rat. 10. If God, ignoring merits, had from mere good pleasure decreed to bless particular persons — say Paul and Peter — then good works would do nothing toward obtaining glory. So let Peter walk in good works: still glory is not credited to him from any desert of those works. Let him neglect good works entirely: God will still give him the destined glory by the force of his good pleasure. That is highly absurd, and leans toward the Predestinarian error Sigebert's Chronicle reports: pious living's good works do not help toward glory if one is not predestinated; flagrant living's crimes do not hurt if one is.
source_text: Rat. 10. Si Deus non habens rationem meritorum, ex solo suo beneplacito decrevisset singulares personas, puta Paulum et Petrum, beare, cum bona opera nihil prorsus operarentur ad gloriam consequendam, Fac igitur Petrum in bonis operibus ambulare, tamen gloria non tribuetur illi ex ullo merito ad talia opera: fac eum bona opera prorsus negligere, Deus tamen virtute beneplaciti sui dabit illi gloriam destinatam: At hoc est valde absurdum, et propendet in errorem Praedestinatorum, quos Sigebertus in Chronico suo ostendit docuisse, Pie viventibus non prodesse bona opera ad gloriam, si Praedestinati non sint; flagitiose viventibus non obesse ulla scelera, si sint ex praedestinatis.
